before.title: GD2/3 melanoma vaccine + anti-PD1 (gilvetmab) for oral malignant melanoma
before.why: Recently diagnosed oral malignant melanoma that has not yet been excised may qualify for combined vaccine/checkpoint immunotherapy.
before.intervention: GD2/3 vaccine plus four IV gilvetmab infusions; serial tumor biopsies and immune monitoring
before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. The study covers the anti-PD-1 drug and study-related tumor biopsies; owners pay for vaccines, exam, staging and other treatment costs.
before.contact: UF Oncology — 352-392-2235; Study Interest Form + referring-veterinarian Oncology Referral Form required
before.notes: Recently diagnosed oral malignant melanoma that is resectable or minimal; dog must NOT have had the oral tumor excised. GD2/3 vaccine is combined with IV gilvetmab. Current UF page explicitly says recruiting.

sites.name: University of Florida College of Veterinary Medicine

original_review.criteria: UF oral-melanoma vaccine+PD1 protocol requires the oral tumor not already excised.

current_review.criteria: UF oral-melanoma vaccine+PD1 protocol requires the oral tumor not already excised. Current full protocol explicitly says the oral tumor must not have been excised; general history of surgery does not prove this. Required diagnostic tumor biopsies are distinct from tumor excision.

cases.name: source-specific contradiction
cases.clinical_scope_correction: Confirmed oral tumor excision is excluded; general unrelated surgery alone does not establish that.

cases.name: Unknown indication of past surgery requires screening
Unrelated surgery does not establish oral tumor excision
Known excised oral melanoma remains excluded

literal_reason: The source prohibits prior excision of the oral melanoma, not every past operation; biopsy itself is mandatory in the study. Specific unknown excision status remains screening, never a Likely match.
